name: NY-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+24 partisan lean makes the district fundamentally out of reach for Republicans
Jeffries combines incumbency, a national profile, and roughly $15M raised against a challenger with no visible funding
Prediction markets price the Democratic side at about 96% to win
No polling or expert ratings; the outlook rests entirely on district fundamentals
model.rationale: A D+24 district, a sitting House party leader with an overwhelming financial edge, and an opponent reporting no fundraising make the fundamentals decisive despite the absence of polling.
model.watch: Turnout in a low-profile race is the main uncertainty; a dramatic national wave or unexpected outside spending against Jeffries could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
The district's partisan lean of roughly 24 points Democratic makes this one of the safest House seats in the country. Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, is seeking another term with about $15 million raised and $5 million on hand. Republican challenger Lewis Mizrahi reports no fundraising, and no outside groups are active in the race. Prediction markets give the Democratic side about a 96 percent chance of holding the seat.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. Those point overwhelmingly to Jeffries, whose incumbency and financial advantage compound already steep partisan terrain. A margin in the high 20s best fits the evidence, and the seat is rated Safe Democratic. Only a dramatic, unforeseen shift would put the outcome in doubt.
